Re-grade (fix round 1) the node:test suite of the meeting-room booking app in /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2. Changed files (testing section's; these ARE the tests, grade test quality as the main item):
- test/helpers/server.mjs, test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs, test/helpers/html.mjs, test/helpers/app.mjs (new)
- test/startup.test.mjs, test/persistence.test.mjs, test/api-routes.test.mjs, test/api-list.test.mjs, test/booking-body.test.mjs, test/booking-fields.test.mjs, test/page-html.test.mjs, test/app-load-list.test.mjs, test/app-submit-cancel.test.mjs
Scratch (grade lightly): .team/scratch/near-miss-defs.mjs, .team/scratch/near-miss-run.mjs.
Spec: .team/notes/spec.md (+ api.md, page.md, decisions.md). Code under test: server.mjs, public/* (not graded).

Previous round: 8/10, fail (duplication 6). Fixes applied since:
- Shared helpers: MSG, expectError, uniqueDate, exists (rethrows non-ENOENT), withTmpDir, withServer in helpers/server.mjs; boot/errorText/NO_REPLY/FAILED/listItems/roomsCall in helpers/app.mjs; local copies removed; chunked POST now uses request({chunks}).
- Timeouts: startServer listening wait (10 s, kills child), request() and rawRequest() socket timeouts (15 s), runToExit 5 s, startup connect-poll loop capped at 500 attempts. package.json is owned by backend; its script is `node --test test/*.test.mjs` — I did not add --test-timeout there since every helper wait is now bounded (judge whether that is enough).
- Order independence: api-list DELETE tests each on their own seeded server; booking-fields '201 shape' tests each on a fresh server; the always-true assert replaced.
- New tests: unexpected 500 (server.mjs copied to a dir without public/ → GET / and /app.js 500 internal error, API keeps working, stdout one line); list-fetch non-string error / {} / body failure; cancel replyLater(404).fail(); cancel stays disabled while body pending; Cancel type 'button' (fake createElement('button') now defaults to type 'submit' like a browser); click() comment fixed.
- html.mjs: only void elements self-close, title/textarea are raw text, character references decoded in text and attributes.
- Invisible characters written as escapes (startup keeps a readable 'données.json' with a comment).
Status: `npm test` 607 pass, 0 fail; all 72 near-miss mutants fail the suite; originals sha256-verified.

User standards: return new objects instead of mutating; small files (200–400 lines, 800 max) and functions (<50 lines); explicit error handling, never swallow; no console.log; exact-equality asserts on spec values; each spec requirement has a test a plausible wrong implementation would fail; deterministic; cleanup.
You may run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2 && npm test`. Do not edit files. Gate: pass = overall ≥ 9 and no item < 7. End with your GRADE block and a file:line fix list.

page.md:30:  - setters: `value` (option, title, filter-date), `textContent` (option, button, #error), `type` (='button' on Cancel), `disabled`
page.md:31:  - getters: `value` (room, title, date, start, end, filter-date), `disabled` (book, Cancel button)
page.md:34:- Listeners registered: form `submit`, #filter-date `change`, #show-all `click`, each Cancel button `click`.
page.md:42:- A click on a disabled Cancel button (or submit while Book disabled) sends nothing.
api.md:28:- 405 replies have no `Allow` header. HEAD and OPTIONS get 405 on known paths.
spec.md:15:- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
spec.md:30:- A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked.
spec.md:34:1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`.
spec.md:50:- Of the browser's APIs, the script uses only `fetch` (with the `method`, `headers` and `body` options, and the reply's `status` and `json()`), `document.getElementById`, `document.createElement`, the `textContent`, `value`, `type`, `disabled`, `append`, `replaceChildren` and `addEventListener` members of elements, and `preventDefault` of events.
spec.md:59:- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
spec.md:61:- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
spec.md:62:- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.

decisions.md:9:- 2026-11-02 — frontend — Clicking an already-disabled Cancel button sends nothing.

content.text:
The suite passes the gate this round: overall 9/10, no item below 8. `npm test` gave 607 pass, 0 fail in about 6 s. I did not re-run the 72 near-miss mutants; that result is your claim.

**What the round 1 fixes changed**
- **Duplication** (6 before) is now 8. The shared helpers in `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/server.mjs` and `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/app.mjs` are used everywhere. `exists` re-throws anything other than ENOENT, and the chunked POST goes through `request({chunks})`. A few small copies are left (listed in the fixes).
- **Order independence** is fixed. The api-list DELETE tests and the booking-fields "201 shape" tests each get their own server. Tests that share a server use `uniqueDate()`, so their bookings never collide.
- **Tests are strong.** Spec messages are matched exactly via `MSG` and `expectError`. Edge cases sit on both sides of each limit: 10000 vs 10001 bytes, multi-byte and chunked bodies, 80 vs 81 title characters with emoji and combining marks, invalid dates, non-Latin digits. Rule order, concurrency, save failures, and the new missing-`public/` 500 test are covered. The fake DOM rejects any API the spec does not allow and logs calls in order, which is how "Book is enabled before anything else" is proved.

**Timeouts: is it enough without `--test-timeout`?** Almost. Every helper wait has a limit except one: `openSocket` sets no socket timeout. So `await ended` in the booking-body "body fully read before reply" tests (lines 223 and 232) would hang forever if the server never closes the connection. Adding a timeout in `openSocket` would close that gap. Otherwise the backend owner needs to add `--test-timeout` to `package.json`.

The few fixed sleeps are acceptable. `delay(300)` in booking-body and `delay(20)`/`delay(100)` in persistence only check that something did *not* happen. Loosening them can only weaken those checks, not make them flaky.

**Other gaps found this round**
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/html.mjs` line 6 still has a raw no-break space in the `nbsp` entry, despite the "invisible characters written as escapes" fix.
- In `booking-fields.test.mjs`, `body()` builds an object and then deletes keys from it. That goes against the "return new objects" standard.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — focused helper modules (server, app, fake-dom, html), small single-purpose functions, shallow nesting; one build-then-delete in booking-fields `body()`
naming: 9 — clear names (expectError, withSeededServer, bootWithError, SETTLERS, NO_REPLY_CASES) that match the spec's wording
duplication: 8 — round 1 helpers removed the big copies; left over: `del` defined in two files, the room-name list written out despite `ROOM_NAMES`, an inline listening regex despite `LISTEN_RE`, `booking-list` childNodes despite `listItems`
size: 9 — largest file 360 lines (startup), all functions well under 50 lines
errors: 9 — `exists` re-throws non-ENOENT, servers and tmp dirs cleaned up in finally, waits bounded except `openSocket`; the swallowed JSON parse in `request()` is documented on purpose
tests: 9 — exact asserts, boundary cases a plausible wrong implementation would fail, rule order, concurrency, save failures, a strict fake DOM, 607/607 passing; one wait with no limit
security: 10 — no secrets; temp dirs only; child env cleaned of the caller's PORT and DATA_FILE
leftovers: 9 — no console or debug code; one raw invisible character in html.mjs
